A +10.0pp gap on the Korea Republic side. Mexico v Korea Republic in FIFA World Cup 2026 is the match. The model has Korea Republic stronger than the market does — that's the reason this fires as a Pick rather than a Pass.

On Elo, Mexico comes in 60 points ahead — Mexico at 1830, Korea Republic at 1770. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. The adjustment layer is quiet on this fixture — no host bonus, no home-ground correction, no altitude folding in. The Elo numbers above are what the model uses.

Three-way split from the model: Mexico to win at 43%, the draw at 26%, and Korea Republic to win at 31%. The away side reads 31% on this distribution — the model's central case for Korea Republic.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Mexico to win at 52%, the draw at 27%, and Korea Republic to win at 20%. The Korea Republic side trades at 20% on Polymarket, which prices out at American odds of +388. That's where the engine differs: our number reads 31%, +10.0pp wider.

The +3pp Pick threshold isn't on the point estimate, it's on the 5th-percentile from a 100-sample bootstrap of the Elo prior plus bonuses. On Korea Republic, that haircut lands the model at 25%; the market is at 20%. Even on the conservative reading, the gap is +4.9pp. The Desk's posture is that calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures — we're not claiming the market is generally wrong, only that this side, on this fixture, looks mispriced. Selection is the dimension this verdict adds value on.

This number will move. Confirmed starting elevens, injuries, weather at the venue, and suspensions carried in from previous fixtures all re-enter the prior on the late-binding cadence. With kickoff 30 days out, we're still on weekly refresh; the daily cadence picks up inside T-5d. The Pick can flip to a Pass if news moves enough of the prior. The Desk does not tip and does not recommend a trade — the model price, the market price, and the gap across them are what's on the page.
drivers: Pre-tournament Elo gives Korea Republic a stronger prior than the Polymarket line implies.
